newsitem.title: USA: Late NYMEX natgas heads up, bulls retake control.
newsitem.headline: Late NYMEX natgas heads up, bulls retake control.

text.p: NYMEX Henry Hub natgas futures, reversing a morning profit-taking slide, mostly headed higher late Friday in moderate activity, buoyed by technical buying when downside momentum stalled early, market sources said.
At 1435 EDT, September climbed 2.1 cents at $2.465 per million British thermal units after dipping early to $2.375. October was 0.8 cent higher at $2.46. Other months were mixed.

"There are a lot of people still trying to fight the (bull) market. There's a perception of a storage problem and the funds are just not ready to liquidate," said one Southwest trader, noting profit taking in the face of softer weekend physical prices pressured the complex this morning.
Most agreed rising concerns about storage after three consecutive unexpectedly-light weekly stock builds helped propel September up almost 16 percent since late July.

Though overall inventories are still 7.5 percent above last year's record lows, they still lag the 1994-1995 average by more than 400 bcf. But some noted weekly injections of just 68 bcf are needed through Oct to get stocks back to 2.8 tcf.

Warmer temperatures are forecast for most of the Northeast, Midwest and southern plains this weekend, with heat expected to remain in parts of the Southwest. However, Southeast weather is forecast to stay below-normal into next week.

Chart traders pegged September resistance at the recent contract high of $2.515, with further selling likely in the spot continuation gap between $2.64 and $2.89 from late January. Support was seen in the $2.34 area and then at $2.30, with better buying likely at $2.25-2.27. Further support points were at $2.20, $2.15-2.16 and then along the short-term up trendline near $2.15.

In the cash Friday, weekend Gulf Coast prices skidded almost 15 cents to the low-to-mid $2.30s. Midcon pipes slipped a similar amount to the mid-$2.20s. New York city gate gas tumbled a dime to the low-$2.50s.
NYMEX volume and open interest figures were unavailable again today due to technical problems at the exchange.
On the KCBT, September firmed two cents to $2.36, while deferreds were steady to six cents higher. The East/West spread widened by 0.1 cent to 10.5 cents (NYMEX premium).
